newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Ghana seeks diplomatic end to Sierra Leone coup.
newsitem.headline: Ghana seeks diplomatic end to Sierra Leone coup.

text.p: Ghana wants to see a return to democracy in Sierra Leone after the May 25 coup but wants to achieve that through negotiation rather than force, the leader of a Ghanaian diplomatic mission to Freetown said.
The delegation, led by deputy foreign minister James Victor Gbeho, finished three days of talks with coup leader Johnny Paul Koroma and other military leaders on Saturday.

"Ghana still supports the OAU (Organisation of African Unity) decision reached in Harare recently, calling on all countries to do their utmost to restore the constitutional order in Sierra Leone," Gbeho told Reuters late on Saturday.
"We believe that the best way to resolve the crisis is by diplomatic means, to reach a negotiated settlement, rather than by fighting," he added.

In a brief declaration to reporters after the talks ended, Koroma said: "We hope that the task that Ghana has undertaken together with us will finally lead to bringing about the restoration of peace, security and constitutional order."
Gbeho said the military government wanted to reach a negotiated settlement to the crisis. "They see our presence here as a window of opportunity and they are ready for talks," he said.
He declined to reveal the substance of the talks with Koroma, who was sworn in as head of state last week.

However, sources close to the talks said the coup leaders had discussed the idea of staying in power for only seven or eight months, rather than the two years they have announced, if an international peace-keeping force, other than the ECOMOG force already in the country, was deployed.
The West African ECOMOG force is led by Nigeria, whose gunboats bombarded Freetown on June 2 in a failed effort to reverse the coup. An anticipated further attack from the Nigerian troops never came.

The new military government wants the former rebels of the Revolutionary United Front, who quickly rallied to the coup, to be given a role in any new government, and is adamant that ousted president Ahmad Tejan Kabbah should not return.
